--- Revisions.md ---
Browsing history
SilverBullet can automatically keep a full revision history of your [[Space]] backed by a [Git](https://git-scm.com/) repository.

--- Log.md ---
Log
To better understand what SilverBullet is doing, especially when [[Troubleshooting]], it is good to know where and how to look at SilverBullet logs.

Start with [[Workbench/Console]] for the combined Lua, JavaScript, plug and service-worker log. For lower-level diagnostics, open your browser’s JavaScript console.

* Client logs: Check your browser’s JavaScript console. Usually these are part of “(Web) Developer Tools” buried somewhere in a Tools or Developer menu.
* Service worker logs (especially useful when debugging [[Sync]] issues):
  * In Chromium-based browsers these logs are mixed with the regular JavaScript console.
  * In Firefox start at `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` then find it under the Service Worker section and click “Inspect”.
  * In Safari they can be accessed via `Developer > Service workers`.
* Server logs: Server logs are written to the standard output of the server process.

--- Share/Collection.md ---
Collection
**Use a target root dedicated to the collection.** When publishing, SilverBullet lists what is under the root, and anything no member maps to is offered for removal: every `.md` file under the root on GitHub, every `.md` file of a gist, and every page under the root on a SilverBullet space. The files are listed unticked, and only those you tick are deleted. A page you renamed shows up as its new file plus the old one in that list.

Where the collection goes:
* **GitHub repository**: a folder in a repository, such as `github:sam-example/moonshot-notes@main/content`. All changes of one publish go into a single commit, and you are asked for its commit message.
* **Gist**: an existing gist, such as `https://gist.github.com/me/abc123`, with each member a file in it.

--- Manual.md ---
Manual
The [[SilverBullet|documentation home]] links to [[Getting Started|Start here]], [[Guides]], [[Administration|Setup and administration]], [[Reference]] and [[Development|Contributing]].

Use Start here for independent introductions, Guides for practical tasks and use cases, and Reference for complete feature behavior and syntax.

--- Install/Server Binary.md ---
Steps | Steps
We start by [downloading the `silverbullet-server-*` zip for your platform from GitHub](https://github.com/silverbulletmd/silverbullet/releases).

Unzip this archive somewhere convenient. You’ll get a single `silverbullet` executable.

Then, create a folder to hold your data (your server configuration and space files will live here):

```bash
mkdir data
```

Run the server, pointing it at that folder:
```bash
./silverbullet data
```

Since `data` is empty, this opens a first-run setup wizard for accounts and your first space — see [[Dashboard]]. Point the server at a folder that already holds pages instead, and it’s served immediately as a classic single space.

The server listens on `http://localhost:3000` by default. To pick a different port, use `-p`:
```bash
./silverbullet -p 3001 data
```

And to bind on an address other than `127.0.0.1` (e.g. to make it reachable on your LAN), use `-L`:
```bash
./silverbullet -L 0.0.0.0 data
```
